title: Pre-Analysis — Damped Aft Mount and Borescope Port for High Utilisation Operation
abstract: Pre-analysis of the third issue aft mount standard, covering the supersession of the spherical bearing, the standalone heat shield window bulletin it invalidates, the fire zone question raised by the borescope port and the crew limitation that sets the duty cycle.

sections.objective: Establish what the damped aft mount and the borescope port supersede or invalidate, whether the port can be cut in the firewall panel without changing the fire zone classification, and whether the mount inspection can genuinely move to a borescope check at each A-check.
sections.scope_note: The search covers ATA 49-10 as the primary chapter and ATA 49-60 as secondary, because the electronic control box shares the tail cone access and its firewall penetration harness is disturbed by the same work. ATA 53-40 was included in the first pass for the tail cone structure and then excluded: the mount bracket is not attached to primary structure at the stations concerned. ATA 26 fire protection was searched for the zone classification reference only.
sections.method_note: Entity linking was seeded from the five part numbers, the four FINs, the two drawings and the four zones. Semantic similarity was run over the operator request and the reason-for-change text of every mount change on this aircraft, and separately over the flight crew limitation set, which entity linking cannot reach. The most useful result came from that second pass: a crew limitation entry that says nothing about mounts but that sets the duty cycle the whole inspection interval assumption rests on. One finding came from entity linking alone, through a single FIN shared with a fault isolation procedure for a completely different system.
sections.findings_summary: Seven items are confirmed and two are blocking. The candidate supersedes the spherical bearing standard, which is itself only three years into a ten year retrofit programme, and the supersession has to be declared carefully or operators part way through will stop and wait. The standalone heat shield window bulletin is the harder problem: it exists specifically so that an operator can take the inspection access without the bearing, and the candidate cuts a second port in a different panel. An aircraft that has taken the standalone bulletin would end up with two openings in the tail cone heat shielding, which the fire zone classification does not currently cover, and that is the blocking certification question. The bearing conversion bulletin has a skip condition for the window that the candidate does not satisfy. Three documentation items follow: the mount inspection task will need a fourth measurement, the illustrated parts figure a fourth state, and the electronic control box fault isolation procedure uses the same access and shares the firewall penetration FIN.
sections.next_steps: Obtain a certification position on the fire zone classification with two openings in the tail cone heat shielding, before any further design work. Establish how many aircraft in the target operators have taken the standalone window bulletin. Agree with the maintenance programme owner whether a borescope check at each A-check can replace the full inspection, because the whole operator benefit depends on it. Draft the supersession statement so that an operator mid-programme is not left uncertain.

similarity_seeds: mount wear scaling with running hours rather than flight hours
inspection access improved by cutting an opening in a heat shield
damping element added in series with a bearing

tasks.title: Trace the mount standard supersession chain
Establish the fire zone position on two heat shield openings
Count aircraft carrying the standalone window bulletin
Assess the borescope check against the full inspection
Review the crew limitation on ground running

evidence.similarity_note: Both describe the aft mount attachment on the same ATA 6D, share four part numbers and three zones, and the candidate re-machines the link the earlier standard produced.

expected_findings.rationale: The spherical bearing standard is three years into a ten year retrofit programme. A supersession declared without care will cause operators mid-programme to stop, and the candidate is targeted at only three operators, so the majority still need the standard being superseded.
expected_findings.resolution: Declare the supersession as applying to the high utilisation population only, and state explicitly that the spherical bearing standard remains the current answer for the rest of the fleet.

expected_findings.rationale: This bulletin exists so that an operator can take the inspection access without the bearing conversion. An aircraft that has taken it and then takes the candidate ends up with two openings in the tail cone heat shielding, in different panels, which the fire zone classification does not cover.
expected_findings.resolution: Obtain a certification position before further design. If two openings cannot be accepted, the candidate must either close the earlier window or adopt it instead of cutting a new port.

expected_findings.rationale: The bearing conversion bulletin carries a skip condition for its own window step when the standalone bulletin has already been done. The candidate does not satisfy that condition because its port is in a different panel, so an aircraft taking all three would have the skip applied incorrectly.
expected_findings.resolution: Amend the skip condition to name the panel rather than the access, and require the candidate to be embodied concurrently with or after the bearing conversion.

expected_findings.rationale: The fault isolation procedure for an auxiliary power unit that will not start puts the firewall penetration harness first, precisely because it is disturbed by mount work and left unsecured. The candidate disturbs the same harness. The two documents share nothing but the FIN: one is about a start failure and the other about bearing wear.
expected_findings.resolution: Add a harness security check to the modification close-out, and reference the fault isolation procedure so that the connection is visible to whoever does the work.

expected_findings.rationale: The task already carries three measurements for three standards and a caution about reading the right one. A fourth standard with a fourth measurement, and a borescope route as well as a direct one, makes it the most error-prone task in the chapter.
expected_findings.resolution: Restructure the task by standard rather than adding a fourth branch, and put the standard identification in a separate preliminary step.

evidence.similarity_note: The crew limitation states that extended ground running is permitted and must be recorded because the installation inspection interval is driven by running hours. That single sentence is the operational basis of the whole utilisation argument behind the candidate, and it contains no part number, no FIN and no reference to a mount.

expected_findings.rationale: The proposed move to a borescope check at each A-check assumes a bounded running hour accumulation between checks. The crew limitation permits unbounded ground running provided it is recorded, so the assumption is not guaranteed by anything the crew are told.
expected_findings.resolution: Either bound the running hours between borescope checks in the maintenance programme, or amend the crew limitation. The certification package must state which.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure already carries three standards as alternates across three sheets. A fourth adds a damped housing and a modified firewall panel with the port, and the effectivity column becomes the only usable ordering reference.
expected_findings.resolution: Split the figure by standard at the next revision rather than adding a fourth alternate set.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned first by every entity search on this mount because it shares three part numbers and both zones, but it is the superseded first standard and no aircraft in the target population is still on it; it has no bearing on the candidate beyond the steel link it introduced.

Surfaces on a semantic search for confined space work in the empennage and does describe an access route with the same difficulties, but it is a fin box rib repair with no shared identifier, no shared zone and nothing to do with the auxiliary power unit installation.

type_data.conclusion: Not yet issued. Two blocking items confirmed and the fire zone classification question is the gate on all further design work.
